status: Implemented; local controls pass. Real-kernel and live-cluster CI proof pending. No qualification credit.
motivation: Loss and one-way partition cases do not exercise packets that arrive late without being dropped. A healthy eventual receipt alone cannot prove that a delay fault was applied or scoped correctly.
existing_shard: chaos-cluster; case count 80; no new shard

fault.selected_process: Capture live leader, both peer IPv4 addresses and process start time. Require the same process during the fault.
fault.scope: Outbound IPv4 UDP to exactly two peers on ports 40201, 40202, 40203, 40204. Each peer has a separate 250 ms netem queue. All unmatched priorities select the undelayed band.
fault.proof: Before/after tc configuration and counters; both peer packet counters increase; no root or peer queue drops; no additional impairment or classifier selectors/actions; two bounded client transfers, 30-second hold, one leader per term, then all three members and progress.
fault.bounds: Four-minute exercise; fifteen-second controller deadline within each remote command; five-minute detached cleanup lease.
fault.ownership: Require existing noqueue root. Exclusive marker records token, device, ifindex, peers and original txqlen. Delete only the owned root. Refuse changed identity, foreign root or unexpected queue-length changes. Restore the original queue length after the Linux automatic zero-to-1000 conversion. An expired old token cannot clear a new fault.

ci_probe.location: Conditional step in the existing chaos-cluster job, before deployment.
ci_probe.environment_change: Load sch_prio, sch_netem and cls_flower on that runner. The node image already supplies iproute2. No product binary, service wiring or runtime configuration changes.
ci_probe.isolation: Outer unshare --net and a child receiver namespace linked with disposable veths. Refuse the initial network namespace. Outer timeout is 60 seconds with a five-second kill grace. The probe disables only the detached lease because namespace destruction bounds its lifetime; controller lease behavior has unit tests.
ci_probe.assertions: Five echo samples for each of two peer Raft UDP flows, a non-Raft port, a non-peer address and TCP. Every delayed sample must be at least 200 ms for the configured 250 ms delay. At least one sample per bypass/restored flow must be below 125 ms. Actual tc counters show traffic without drops; noqueue and original txqlen are restored.
ci_probe.artifact: /tmp/chaos-raft-delay-kernel.json; existing chaos JSON artifact upload. Timing thresholds validate the fault injector, not product latency.

local_validation.chaos: 316 passed, 2 ignored on the final tree based on integration 07efb09d.
local_validation.python_controller: 9 tests pass. Exact embedded Python source under modeled ip/tc commands; this is not a kernel test.
local_validation.style: just style passes; existing proc-macro-error2 future-incompatibility notice remains.
local_validation.local_limit: This host denies unprivileged network namespaces and lacks passwordless sudo. No local live cluster or privileged container was started.

performance: No product hot-path change. The deliberate 250 ms Raft delay belongs only to this chaos fault. Deployed latency/throughput nonregression and ten consecutive final-head full CI rounds remain unproven.
